Thanks — I can do that. A couple quick clarifying choices before I run anything (I’ll preserve formulas by default and create a backup unless you tell me otherwise):

Proposed safe workflow (recommended)
- Create a backup sheet (e.g., Vendors_backup_timestamp) so nothing is lost.
- Inspect both 2024 and 2025 sheets to find duplicates (trim spaces, case-insensitive name match).
- Add a helper column on each sheet (e.g., DEDUP_FLAG) marking rows judged duplicates and showing the matching row(s).
- Build a single deduped master sheet (or replace in-place) with one canonical row per vendor.
- Update summary references if needed so totals come from the deduped data (I will preserve existing formulas unless you ask me to change them).

Decisions I need from you
1) Matching rule for duplicates:
   - Option A (default): Exact-match on vendor name, case-insensitive, trimmed.
   - Option B: Treat names as duplicates only if both name and vendor ID match.
   - Option C: Use name match as primary; if names match but vendor IDs differ, flag for manual review (recommended).
Which do you want?

2) When name matches but vendor ID differs:
   - Keep both (leave flagged for review).
   - Keep the row that has a vendor ID (drop the one missing an ID).
   - Keep one and merge fields (specify which sheet/fields to prefer).
Which behavior do you prefer?

3) Where should the canonical row live after dedupe?
   - Keep deduped rows in 2025 (remove duplicates from 2024).
   - Create a new sheet called Vendors_dedup (recommended).
   - Overwrite both sheets (not recommended).

If you confirm the defaults (backup + name-based exact match, flag mismatch on vendor ID, create new Vendors_dedup sheet), I’ll inspect the 2024 and 2025 sheets now and then run the dedupe. Proceed?
